obligations.cadence_note: Not periodic at all — the document requires CONTINUOUS real-time monitoring, so there is no interval to age against. This obligation cannot go 'overdue' in the usual sense; the failure mode is a monitoring outage or a gap in the data feed, which is a different alert and needs modelling as such.
obligations.applies_to: All buildings and facilities in scope — continuous real-time IAQ monitoring, not a periodic sample.
obligations.source_quote: "Indoor air quality parameters shall be monitored continuously using IoT-enabled or any smart sensors that provide real-time data transmission." (Appendix-1, General Requirements, item 1, page 16.) Continuous monitoring has no cadence in months or days.

obligations.cadence_note: These are AVERAGING WINDOWS (1-hour, 8-hour, 24-hour), not recurrence intervals for an obligation. Deliberately not mapped onto cadence_days — doing so would make the engine expect a fresh submission every hour, which the document does not require.
obligations.applies_to: Exposure averaging windows required for assessment and reporting.
obligations.source_quote: "1-hour averaging for immediate risk assessment and compliance with short-term exposure limits (STELs). 8-hour and 24-hour averaging for long-term IAQ trend analysis and regulatory compliance." (Appendix-1, item 2, page 16.) Also §7-2-1: "Sampling duration: Continuous real-time monitoring or periodic sampling over a minimum of 8 hours to capture variations." (page 9).

obligations.cadence_note: THE DOCUMENT IS SILENT on frequency — it says 'routine calibration and performance validation' and stops there. Contrast GU119, which does fix six-monthly for parking CO sensors and at least annual for air quality testing equipment; if a client is entitled to both modules, the GU119 cadence is the defensible one to apply to shared equipment.
obligations.applies_to: Calibration and performance validation of all IAQ monitoring devices and sensors.
obligations.source_quote: "All IAQ monitoring devices and sensors shall be: Calibrated and certified in accordance with ISO 17025. Subject to routine calibration and performance validation by accredited laboratories or authorized service providers." (Appendix-1, item 4, page 17.) 'Routine' is not quantified — no cadence is stated.

obligations.cadence_note: THE DOCUMENT NAMES THREE INTERVALS AT ONCE — 'hourly, daily, monthly' — and does not say which applies to whom, so no single cadence can be derived. If this is sold, the interval must be agreed with the client and stored as a client-specific value. The five-year retention period in the same clause is a separate, unambiguous requirement and should be modelled as retention, not cadence.
obligations.applies_to: Automatic generation and submission of IAQ compliance reports.
obligations.source_quote: "IAQ compliance reports must be automatically generated at predefined intervals (hourly, daily, monthly) and submitted to the relevant regulatory authority for oversight and enforcement when required." (Appendix-1, item 5, page 17.) Three intervals are named together, so no single cadence is encodable. Same item: "IAQ monitoring data shall be securely stored for a minimum period of five (5) years to ensure regulatory auditability."
